description: GDIS, a global dataset of geocoded disaster locations is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Elisabeth L. Rosvold et al. This article presents a new open source extension to the Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) that allows researchers, for the first time, to explore and make use of subnational, geocoded data on major disasters triggered by natural hazards. Coverage: global; published in 2021. Formats: CSV, GeoPackage. The data are held in Palisades, NY: NASA Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center (SEDAC) and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support emergency-service and public-facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
